title: The Integration Boost is priced per block against the Sky Savings Rate, tying the subsidy to Sky's own cost of funds
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.1.7 specifies the Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy: "The Integration Boost is calculated based on per block values for USDS in Aave and the Sky Savings Rate."

Two choices are packed into that sentence. Measuring **per block** means the reward tracks the actual time-weighted balance rather than a snapshot, which removes the standard attack of parking capital only at the moment of measurement. Benchmarking to the **Sky Savings Rate** means the subsidy is expressed relative to the yield Sky already offers USDS holders directly.

The benchmark is what makes the mechanism economically coherent. Sky's alternative to incentivizing Aave deposits is simply paying the Savings Rate to holders itself; pricing the boost off that rate means the ecosystem is comparing two routes to the same objective on a common basis, rather than setting an arbitrary emissions budget.

It also makes the subsidy self-adjusting. When the Savings Rate falls, the boost falls with it, so the incentive programme cannot drift out of line with the ecosystem's own cost of funds — a failure mode of fixed-budget liquidity mining, where incentives stay large after the economics that justified them have changed.
description: Rewards are computed from per-block USDS balances in Aave and the Sky Savings Rate, so the incentive tracks what Sky already pays savers instead of being a fixed budget.
